title: Common definitions
description: Shared primitive types referenced by all Yeonjae Studio schemas. Text fields are language-neutral; where the language may vary, an explicit language code accompanies the text. Manuscript text is English (OUTPUT-EN-001).

languageCode.description: BCP 47 language tag, e.g. en, en-US, en-GB, ko

manuscriptLanguage.description: The manuscript language. Composition is direct in this language (ADR-0054); English is an explicit later translation surface. Enforced per project by the identity contract.

spellingLocale.description: Spelling and punctuation locale for the manuscript language (en-US, en-GB, ko-KR)

text.description: UTF-8, NFC-normalized text. Working text (plans, canon statements, issues) is English; the language of user-authored text is recorded alongside it where it may vary.

localizedText.description: User-authored text with its language code and an optional English working paraphrase used in prompts.

text_en.description: English working paraphrase when language != en (never manuscript text)

lengthModel.description: Language-neutral length measurement (ADR-0034). For English manuscripts, words is the author-facing primary unit.

code_points.description: Unicode code points after NFC, including spaces, excluding markup

lengthTarget.description: Author-facing length target. Unit is words for English; tolerance is a ratio.

storyClock.description: Position in story time (ADR-0040). Two orderings: NARRATIVE order (chapter_no, ordinal) is total within a timeline and always present; WORLD order (calendar + world_date) is partial and used only when both clocks share a calendar and neither has precision=unknown. Facts and events sort by narrative order (derived key ord = chapter_no*1e6 + ordinal); world_date resolves flashbacks and elapsed-time checks. Clocks on different timelines are comparable only through the child timeline's divergence clock.

chapter_no.description: Chapter during whose story-present this moment occurs. 0 = before chapter 1 (backstory, flashback material, prior-loop or source-story events whose story-present precedes the manuscript).

ordinal.description: Order within the chapter's story-present, assigned by the extractor (paragraph order of the anchoring evidence by default). Equal ordinals mean simultaneous or unordered; ties break deterministically by item id.

calendar.description: Calendar system of world_date: 'gregorian', 'relative_days' (D+35 / D-10 from the story's day zero), or 'era:<name>' for in-world calendars. world_date values are comparable only within one calendar.

world_date.description: In-world date/time in the stated calendar (ISO-8601 for gregorian; D±n[Thh:mm] for relative_days; free era-relative string otherwise)

precision.description: Certainty of world_date. unknown = no usable world position (narrative order only; reported as a continuity risk when a duration check needs it).

uncertainty_days.description: Half-width of the plausible window when precision=approx

realityFrame.description: See ADR-0007 and ADR-0039. Fact-bearing frames: canonical and flashback (main or current timeline), prior_loop, alternate_timeline and source_story (each on its own timeline). lie/dream/hallucination/hypothetical/prediction produce knowledge only; plan lives only in plan tables; non_canonical_draft never enters canon.

qualityDimension.description: Separate evaluation dimensions (EVAL-SEPARATION-001). prose = English prose quality; structure = Korean-webnovel structural adherence.

evidenceRef.description: Exact span into an immutable manuscript version. start/end are Unicode code-point offsets into the NFC text (ADR-0030); quote must equal the code-point slice text[start:end].

paragraph_id.description: Stable paragraph id within the version, e.g. p14

knowerRef.description: A character entity or a pseudo-knower.

registerLevel.description: Abstract register axis value (0 = lowest/most casual, 4 = highest/most formal or deferential)

dialogueRegister.description: Abstract canonical description of how a speaker addresses a counterpart, rendered in natural English by the writer (replaces Korean speech-level enforcement).

address_terms.description: English vocatives/references the speaker uses for the counterpart, e.g. 'Senior Park', 'sir', 'Do-yoon'

materiality.description: Dependency edge class (ADR-0032). Only material edges mark dependents stale by default.

timelineKind.description: Timeline kinds (ADR-0023, ADR-0039). prior_loop, alternate and source_story timelines carry their own facts; the main timeline learns of them only through knowledge stances.

manuscriptStatus.description: Manuscript-version lifecycle (ADR-0037): working (draft/candidate/revision under production) → approved (approval-locked for extraction; immutable input to canon extraction) → accepted (set inside the atomic canon commit) → superseded (a regeneration was accepted) | retconned (a retcon version was accepted); rejected versions move to quarantine.

manuscriptOrigin.description: How a manuscript version came to exist (content provenance, orthogonal to status): assembled from scene drafts, produced by a patch (revision), one of N candidates, a retcon edit of an accepted version, or imported text.
